claims.text: The starting material is an as-cast HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy contains Hf, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr at approximately equal atomic percentages.
Design of experiments methodology can be used to systematically vary the elemental percentages.
The composition range is plus or minus 10% relative to the equal-percentage baseline.
The compositions will be tested under uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature.
Changing elemental percentages changes lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing elemental percentages changes solid-solution strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening influence the alloy's mechanical properties.
Yield strength and hardness will vary predictably with systematic changes in elemental percentages.
Increasing the Hf percentage by 10% and decreasing the Ti percentage by 5% will increase yield strength by 15% relative to baseline.
Increasing the Hf percentage by 10% and decreasing the Ti percentage by 5% will increase hardness by 20% relative to baseline.
The equal-atomic-percentage as-cast baseline has a yield strength of 800 MPa.
The equal-atomic-percentage as-cast baseline has a hardness of 350 HV.
Beyond the plus or minus 10% composition range, the microstructure and mechanical properties may deviate significantly from the predicted behavior.
Processing conditions, impurities, and experimental errors may cause the measured properties to differ from the predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if yield strength and hardness differ by more than 10% from predicted values for at least 80% of tested compositions.
